i18n.en: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ye'or* (הַיְאֹר) — the Hebrew word standardly rendered 'the river' here is the Bible's distinctive name for the Nile, an Egyptian loanword (Eg. *itrw* / *iaru*, 'great river / canal'). Outside Pharaoh's-dream context the noun is reserved almost exclusively for the Nile across the corpus — the plague-narratives (Exod 7-8 extensively), the prophetic Egypt-oracles (Isa 19; Ezek 29-32; Amos 8-9; Nahum 3) — making it a recognized authentic Egyptian-court-milieu detail of the Yosef-cycle (Vergote, Redford). The Nile-bank reed-marsh sense (against the older 'meadow' rendering of KJV) is the philologically accurate register and the ASV's choice here. The cluster of Egyptian loanwords (*Ye'or*, *achu*) packs the dream-vision with authentic Nile-Delta vocabulary.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶׁ֧בַע פָּר֣וֹת אֲחֵר֗וֹת עֹל֤וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶן֙ מִן־הַיְאֹ֔ר רָע֥וֹת מַרְאֶ֖ה וְדַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֛דְנָה אֵ֥צֶל הַפָּר֖וֹת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill-favored and lean-fleshed, and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּאכַ֣לְנָה הַפָּר֗וֹת רָע֤וֹת הַמַּרְאֶה֙ וְדַקֹּ֣ת הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַפָּר֔וֹת יְפֹ֥ת הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְהַבְּרִיאֹ֑ת וַיִּיקַ֖ץ פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And the ill-favored and lean-fleshed kine did eat up the seven well-favored and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּישָׁ֕ן וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֖ם שֵׁנִ֑ית וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹל֛וֹת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד בְּרִיא֥וֹת וְטֹבֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And he slept and dreamed a second time: and, behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, rank and good.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים דַּקּ֖וֹת וּשְׁדוּפֹ֣ת קָדִ֑ים צֹמְח֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶֽן׃

i18n.en: And, behold, seven ears, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּבְלַ֙עְנָה֙ הַשִּׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקּ֔וֹת אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִ֔ים הַבְּרִיא֖וֹת וְהַמְּלֵא֑וֹת וַיִּיקַ֥ץ פַּרְעֹ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֲלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, it was a dream.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וַתִּפָּ֣עֶם רוּח֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־כָּל־חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֶת־כָּל־חֲכָמֶ֑יהָ וַיְסַפֵּ֨ר פַּרְעֹ֤ה לָהֶם֙ אֶת־חֲלֹמ֔וֹ וְאֵין־פּוֹתֵ֥ר אוֹתָ֖ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Mitsrayim, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Chartumim* (חַרְטֻמֵּי), rendered ASV-baseline 'magicians', is an Egyptian loanword from Eg. *ḥr(y)-tp* ('chief lector-priest'), the senior class of ritual specialists of the *per-ankh* ('house of life') temple-scriptoria — sacred scribes, ritual-text readers, dream-interpreters. The lemma is a major cross-corpus node: it recurs through Exod 7-9 (the Egyptian magicians vs Moshe and Aharon — explicit conceptual link to this scene), and across Dan 1-2, 4-5 (the Babylonian / Chaldean *chartumim* of Nebuchadnezzar's court).

*Tippa'em rucho* (וַתִּפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ) — 'his spirit was troubled' (lit. 'his spirit was beaten / pulsed') — uses the verb *pa'am* (pulse, beat, strike) in the Niphal of disturbed inner-state. The same idiom recurs only at Dan 2:1, 2:3, of Nebuchadnezzar's troubled spirit at his own dream — the closest HB literary parallel, framing the two great Gentile-king dream-and-interpreter sequences (Sarna, Alter).

The verse opens the chapter's dream-interpretation cluster (*pitron* / verb *p-t-r*, vv 8, 11, 12, 13, 15) which is the same Gen 40-41 keyword cluster the central entry governs.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֶת־חֲטָאַ֕י אֲנִ֖י מַזְכִּ֥יר הַיּֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:

paragraphs.commentary: The chief butler's *mazkir hayyom* ('I do remember this day') answers the *va-yishkachehu* ('and he forgat him') of Gen 40:23 — the cupbearer who forgot Yosef now remembers. The verbal echo (the *z-k-r* / *sh-k-ch* remember/forget pair that closes Gen 40 and reopens here) is editorially deliberate.

paragraphs.text: פַּרְעֹ֖ה קָצַ֣ף עַל־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתִ֜י בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֚ית שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים אֹתִ֕י וְאֵ֖ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִֽים׃

i18n.en: Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in ward in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker:

paragraphs.text: וַנַּֽחַלְמָ֥ה חֲל֛וֹם בְּלַ֥יְלָה אֶחָ֖ד אֲנִ֣י וָה֑וּא אִ֛ישׁ כְּפִתְר֥וֹן חֲלֹמ֖וֹ חָלָֽמְנוּ׃

i18n.en: and we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁ֨ם אִתָּ֜נוּ נַ֣עַר עִבְרִ֗י עֶ֚בֶד לְשַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים וַנְּ֨סַפֶּר־ל֔וֹ וַיִּפְתָּר־לָ֖נוּ אֶת־חֲלֹמֹתֵ֑ינוּ אִ֥ישׁ כַּחֲלֹמ֖וֹ פָּתָֽר׃

i18n.en: And there was with us there a young man, an Ivri, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.

paragraphs.commentary: *Na'ar Ivri* ('a young man, an Ivri') triples the cupbearer's distancing of Yosef: *na'ar* (subordinate / lad), *Ivri* (the outsider's gentilic — see the central `ha-ivri-hebrew-etymology`), *eved le-sar ha-tabbachim* ('servant to the captain of the guard'). The phrasing renders Yosef triply marked as low-status before Pharaoh; the cupbearer's voice is unmistakably that of a courtier reporting on a useful foreign slave, not of a friend recommending a peer. The narrow Gen 37:2 overlay `naar-lad-youth-or-attendant` is NOT extended to this verse — the Gen 37 entry governs a chapter-specific syntactic ambiguity (*ve-hu na'ar et-benei...*) absent here.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּֽתַר־לָ֖נוּ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֑ה אֹתִ֛י הֵשִׁ֥יב עַל־כַּנִּ֖י וְאֹת֥וֹ תָלָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח פַּרְעֹה֙ וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְרִיצֻ֖הוּ מִן־הַבּ֑וֹר וַיְגַלַּח֙ וַיְחַלֵּ֣ף שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: Then Pharaoh sent and called Yosef, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Min ha-bor* — 'out of the dungeon' — is the third and last Yosef-cycle prison-as-*bor* reference, deliberately echoing the dry cistern of Gen 37:24, 28 (the brothers' pit) and Yosef's retrospective at 40:15 (*ha-bor*, the Egyptian prison). The same lemma resolves the cycle: Yosef is drawn 'up' (*va-yeritzuhu*, hastily) from the pit, exactly the verbal action by which he was drawn up at Gen 37:28.

*Va-yegallach va-yechallef simlotav* ('he shaved and changed his garments') — the shaving is an Egyptian-court detail: Egyptian priests and senior courtiers were ritually clean-shaven, in deliberate contrast to the bearded Semitic practice (Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* 1959; Redford *A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph* 1970). Yosef's preparation to enter Pharaoh's presence requires both the shave and a change of clothes — the same garment-replacement motif that has marked his major transitions (the *ketonet passim* of Gen 37, stripped; his outer garment at Gen 39, seized by Potifar's wife).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְתִּי וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַאֲנִ֗י שָׁמַ֤עְתִּי עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תִּשְׁמַ֥ע חֲל֖וֹם לִפְתֹּ֥ר אֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto Yosef, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that when thou hearest a dream thou canst interpret it.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨עַן יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֛ה לֵאמֹ֖ר בִּלְעָדָ֑י אֱלֹהִ֕ים יַעֲנֶ֖ה אֶת־שְׁל֥וֹם פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: Elohim shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.

paragraphs.commentary: *Bil'adai* — 'It is not in me' (literally 'apart from me') — opens Yosef's disclaimer-then-redirect: he refuses the credit (*bil'adai*) and points it to Elohim. This is the cycle's Elohim-default reasserting itself outside the Gen 39 YHWH-frame (governed by the overlay `yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim`); Pharaoh's court is the natural register for the more general *Elohim*, paralleling Yosef's *le-Elohim* at 39:9 and 40:8. ASV-baseline 'It is not in me' retained.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף בַּחֲלֹמִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י עֹמֵ֖ד עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh spake unto Yosef, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the brink of the river:

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִן־הַיְאֹ֗ר עֹלֹת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פָּר֔וֹת בְּרִיא֥וֹת בָּשָׂ֖ר וִיפֹ֣ת תֹּ֑אַר וַתִּרְעֶ֖ינָה בָּאָֽחוּ׃

i18n.en: and, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fat-fleshed and well-favored; and they fed in the reed-grass:

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶֽׁבַע־פָּר֤וֹת אֲחֵרוֹת֙ עֹל֣וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן דַּלּ֨וֹת וְרָע֥וֹת תֹּ֛אַר מְאֹ֖ד וְרַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר לֹֽא־רָאִ֧יתִי כָהֵ֛נָּה בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לָרֹֽעַ׃

i18n.en: and, behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very ill-favored and lean-fleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Mitsrayim for badness:

paragraphs.commentary: Pharaoh's retelling departs from the narrator's leaner first-person account at vv 1-7 by adding affective intensifiers: the new adjective *dallot* ('poor') beyond the narrator's *daqqot* ('lean', v 3); the explicit superlative *lo-ra'iti khahennah be-khol eretz Mitsrayim la-roa* ('such as I never saw in all the land of Mitsrayim for badness'). The narrator-vs-character retelling-variation is a recognized literary observation (Sarna, Alter): the narrator's prose is taut and visual; Pharaoh's retelling lingers, intensifies, recoils. The same pattern repeats at vv 21 (the eaten cattle remaining ill-favored, a detail absent from v 4) and v 23 (the hapax *tzenumot*, 'withered', absent from v 6).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּאכַ֙לְנָה֙ הַפָּר֔וֹת הָרַקּ֖וֹת וְהָרָע֑וֹת אֵ֣ת שֶׁ֧בַע הַפָּר֛וֹת הָרִאשֹׁנ֖וֹת הַבְּרִיאֹֽת׃

i18n.en: and the lean and ill-favored kine did eat up the first seven fat kine:

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה אֶל־קִרְבֶּ֗נָה וְלֹ֤א נוֹדַע֙ כִּי־בָ֣אוּ אֶל־קִרְבֶּ֔נָה וּמַרְאֵיהֶ֣ן רַ֔ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּתְּחִלָּ֑ה וָאִיקָֽץ׃

i18n.en: and when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they were still ill-favored, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

paragraphs.text: וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲלֹמִ֑י וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹלֹ֛ת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד מְלֵאֹ֥ת וְטֹבֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up upon one stalk, full and good:

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים צְנֻמ֥וֹת דַּקּ֖וֹת שְׁדֻפ֣וֹת קָדִ֑ים צֹמְח֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: and, behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them:

paragraphs.commentary: *Tzenumot* (צְנֻמוֹת) — 'withered' — is a hapax legomenon, occurring only here in the HB, and absent from the narrator's first account of the dream at v 6. The root *tz-n-m* is otherwise unattested in BH; proposed cognates (Arabic *ṣanama*, 'to be hard, dry'; Aramaic / Akkadian comparanda) are suggestive but not decisive. The ASV 'withered' is the dominant English rendering and the principal contextual reading; the hapax-status and lack of secure cognate evidence are documented in the overlay glossary entry (see `tzenumot-withered-hapax-gen41`).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּבְלַ֙עְןָ֙ הָשִׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקֹּ֔ת אֵ֛ת שֶׁ֥בַע הַֽשִׁבֳּלִ֖ים הַטֹּב֑וֹת וָֽאֹמַר֙ אֶל־הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַגִּ֖יד לִֽי׃

i18n.en: and the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears: and I told it unto the magicians; but there was none that could declare it to me.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה חֲל֥וֹם פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶחָ֣ד ה֑וּא אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הִגִּ֥יד לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: what the Elohim is about to do he hath declared unto Pharaoh.

paragraphs.text: שֶׁ֧בַע פָּרֹ֣ת הַטֹּבֹ֗ת שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִים֙ הַטֹּבֹ֔ת שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים הֵ֑נָּה חֲל֖וֹם אֶחָ֥ד הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.

paragraphs.text: וְשֶׁ֣בַע הַ֠פָּרוֹת הָֽרַקּ֨וֹת וְהָרָעֹ֜ת הָעֹלֹ֣ת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ן שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִׁבֳּלִים֙ הָרֵק֔וֹת שְׁדֻפ֖וֹת הַקָּדִ֑ים יִהְי֕וּ שֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י רָעָֽב׃

i18n.en: And the seven lean and ill-favored kine that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind; they shall be seven years of famine.

paragraphs.text: ה֣וּא הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הֶרְאָ֥ה אֶת־פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: That is the thing which I spake unto Pharaoh: what the Elohim is about to do he hath showed unto Pharaoh.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֛ה שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים בָּא֑וֹת שָׂבָ֥ע גָּד֖וֹל בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Mitsrayim:

paragraphs.text: וְ֠קָמוּ שֶׁ֨בַע שְׁנֵ֤י רָעָב֙ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן וְנִשְׁכַּ֥ח כָּל־הַשָּׂבָ֖ע בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְכִלָּ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ב אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Mitsrayim; and the famine shall consume the land;

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־יִוָּדַ֤ע הַשָּׂבָע֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֛י הָרָעָ֥ב הַה֖וּא אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֑ן כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד ה֖וּא מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: and the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine which followeth; for it shall be very grievous.

paragraphs.text: וְעַ֨ל הִשָּׁנ֧וֹת הַחֲל֛וֹם אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה פַּעֲמָ֑יִם כִּֽי־נָכ֤וֹן הַדָּבָר֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמְמַהֵ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh, it is because the thing is established by the Elohim, and the Elohim will shortly bring it to pass.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef articulates the doubled-dream principle explicitly: *al hishshanot ha-chalom el-Par'oh pa'amayim ki nakhon ha-davar me-im ha-Elohim u-memaher ha-Elohim la'asoto* — 'and for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh, it is because the thing is established by the Elohim, and the Elohim will shortly bring it to pass.' Two interpretive claims are folded into one sentence: doubling signals *certainty* (*nakhon*, 'established / fixed / set'), and doubling signals *imminence* (*memaher*, 'hastening'). The principle is the cycle's stated theology of the symbolic dream — and a sibling-node to the central `pitron-dream-interpretation-yosef-cycle` entry. The principle resonates back to the doubled dreams of Gen 37 (Yosef's sheaves + stars), the cupbearer-baker pair of Gen 40, and the Pharaoh cattle-and-ears pair of this chapter; forward to Dan 2 (Nebuchadnezzar's two-stage dream) and the broader rabbinic dream-theology. Documented in the new overlay entry `dream-doubling-as-confirmation-gen41`.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יֵרֶ֣א פַרְעֹ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ נָב֣וֹן וְחָכָ֑ם וִישִׁיתֵ֖הוּ עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary: *Navon ve-chakham* ('discreet and wise', or 'understanding and wise') — the doublet of the wisdom-formula. *Navon* (n-b-n, 'understanding, prudent, discerning') + *chakham* ('wise, skilled') is a stock pairing recurring at Deut 1:13, 4:6; throughout Proverbs; and in the post-exilic wisdom register. ASV 'discreet and wise' preserves the older register; modern renderings vary ('intelligent', 'prudent'). The pairing recurs at v 39 in Pharaoh's response, making the formula the structural pivot of the elevation-scene.

paragraphs.text: יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה פַרְעֹ֔ה וְיַפְקֵ֥ד פְּקִדִ֖ים עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחִמֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י הַשָּׂבָֽע׃

i18n.en: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Mitsrayim in the seven plenteous years.

paragraphs.commentary: *Chimmesh* (וְחִמֵּשׁ), the Piel of ch-m-sh, is a genuine philological crux. Two readings compete: (a) the **tax-reading** — 'take up the fifth part', i.e., institute a 20% grain-tax on the harvest; cognate to *chamishit*, 'fifth'; the dominant tradition (ASV / KJV / NJPS) and the natural reading given the grain-storage program of vv 35-36. (b) The **administrative reading** — 'organize / muster in five [divisions]'; cognate to *chamushim* ('in battle-array', 'in fives', the Exodus march-formation); on this reading the verb is a derived sense to deploy by fives, and Yosef proposes restructuring the country into administrative fifths. ASV-baseline 'take up the fifth part' is retained; the contested administrative-reading is documented in the overlay entry.

paragraphs.text: וְיִקְבְּצ֗וּ אֶת־כָּל־אֹ֙כֶל֙ הַשָּׁנִ֣ים הַטֹּבֹ֔ת הַבָּאֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְיִצְבְּרוּ־בָ֞ר תַּ֧חַת יַד־פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֹ֥כֶל בֶּעָרִ֖ים וְשָׁמָֽרוּ׃

i18n.en: And let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֨ה הָאֹ֤כֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ לְשֶׁ֙בַע֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹֽא־תִכָּרֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּרָעָֽב׃

i18n.en: And the food shall be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Mitsrayim; that the land perish not through the famine.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּיטַ֥ב הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־עֲבָדָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־עֲבָדָ֑יו הֲנִמְצָ֣א כָזֶ֔ה אִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֛ר ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom the spirit of Elohim is?

paragraphs.commentary: *Ish asher ruach Elohim bo* — 'a man in whom the spirit of Elohim is' — deploys the *ruach Elohim* formula in its **in-a-person** sense, distinct phenomenologically from the cosmic *ruach Elohim* of Gen 1:2 (the breath/wind hovering over the waters). The in-a-person *ruach* is the HB's standard register for charismatic wisdom, prophetic capacity, or craft-skill: Betzalel filled with the *ruach Elohim* of wisdom for the tabernacle (Exod 31:3, 35:31); the seventy elders sharing Moshe's *ruach* (Num 11:17, 25); the *ruach* upon Bil'am (Num 24:2); the *ruach YHWH* upon the judges and the messianic figure (Judg 3:10; 6:34; 11:29; 13:25; 14:6; 14:19; 15:14; Isa 11:2). The new overlay entry `ruach-elohim-in-a-person-gen41` houses the in-a-person sense as a sibling to the central `ruach-elohim` (Gen 1:2) entry — both renderings preserved, no harmonization. Pharaoh's recognition is **functional** (the discernment Yosef just displayed); the deeper theological cluster is documented in apparatus.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אַחֲרֵ֨י הוֹדִ֧יעַ אֱלֹהִ֛ים אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶת־כָּל־זֹ֑את אֵין־נָב֥וֹן וְחָכָ֖ם כָּמֽוֹךָ׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto Yosef, Forasmuch as Elohim hath showed thee all of this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou:

paragraphs.commentary: Pharaoh's response echoes Yosef's own *navon ve-chakham* formula of v 33: the king accepts the proposal and elevates the proposer. The chiastic echo (Yosef proposes a *navon ve-chakham*; Pharaoh declares Yosef himself the *navon ve-chakham*) is the structural pivot of the elevation.

paragraphs.text: אַתָּה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה עַל־בֵּיתִ֔י וְעַל־פִּ֖יךָ יִשַּׁ֣ק כָּל־עַמִּ֑י רַ֥ק הַכִּסֵּ֖א אֶגְדַּ֥ל מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

i18n.en: thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.

paragraphs.commentary: *Al pikha yishshaq kol ammi* — ASV 'shall all my people be ruled' — turns on a genuinely ambiguous verb *yishshaq*. Three readings compete: (a) the **homage-by-obedience reading** — 'shall be ruled / governed by thy word', taking *yishshaq* as a derived sense of *nashaq* ('to kiss' = render homage by kissing; cf. 1 Sam 10:1; Ps 2:12); the ASV/KJV tradition. (b) The **literal kiss-the-mouth reading** — 'shall kiss thy mouth', taking the kiss as the homage-gesture itself (Alter). (c) The **arm/equip reading** — some commentators emend or read *nashaq* in the sense 'to arm / equip with weapons' (cf. *neshek*, 'weapon', 1 Chr 12:2 *noshqei qeshet*), giving 'shall arm themselves at thy word'. The crux is recognized; ASV-baseline 'shall be ruled' retained; readings documented in the overlay entry `al-pikha-yishshaq-shall-be-ruled-philological-crux-gen41`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי אֹֽתְךָ֔ עַ֖ל כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto Yosef, See, I have set thee over all the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֨סַר פַּרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־טַבַּעְתּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל יָד֔וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֖הּ עַל־יַ֣ד יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיַּלְבֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ בִּגְדֵי־שֵׁ֔שׁ וַיָּ֛שֶׂם רְבִ֥ד הַזָּהָ֖ב עַל־צַוָּארֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it upon Yosef's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;

paragraphs.commentary:
*Bigdei-shesh* ('vestures of *shesh*-linen') — *shesh* (שֵׁשׁ) is an Egyptian loanword (Eg. *šs*) denoting the fine white Egyptian linen of priests and royalty. The lemma is a major cross-corpus node: it saturates the tabernacle / priestly vestment instructions of Exod 25-39 (*shesh moshzar*, 'twisted fine linen'), recurs in Esther (1:6; 8:15), and in Ezek 27:7 of the high-status Egyptian textile-trade. Yosef's investiture in *bigdei-shesh* marks him sartorially as Egyptian-court elite — the textile complements the gold-collar (*revid ha-zahav*, see commentary below) and the signet ring as the three elements of senior-officer investiture known from Egyptian tomb-reliefs.

*Revid ha-zahav* ('a gold chain') — the noun *ravid* is rare (the only other HB occurrence is Ezek 16:11 of a jewelry-piece) and is widely identified with the **Egyptian *shebyu*-collar**, the gold collar-of-honor depicted on tomb-reliefs as the public ceremonial reward bestowed by the king on senior officials at investiture-ceremonies of exactly the kind staged here (Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* 1959 pp. 121-135; Redford 1970; standard Egyptological treatments of the *shebyu*-of-gold investiture-protocol). ASV-baseline 'a gold chain' retained; the Egyptological identification documented in apparatus.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּרְכֵּ֣ב אֹת֗וֹ בְּמִרְכֶּ֤בֶת הַמִּשְׁנֶה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ לְפָנָ֖יו אַבְרֵ֑ךְ וְנָת֣וֹן אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ל כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he set him over all the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary:
Two cruxes occupy this verse.

*Mirkevet ha-mishneh* ('the second chariot') — the construct *mishneh* ('second / deputy / second-in-command') yields two readings: (a) the **ordinal reading** — 'the second chariot', i.e., the chariot ranking immediately after Pharaoh's own (ASV/KJV); (b) the **office-title reading** — 'the chariot of the second-in-command / the deputy', taking *mishneh* as the office-title (the Egyptian vizier-office, cf. 2 Chr 28:7 of the king's *mishneh* as deputy; Esth 10:3 of Mordekhai as *mishneh la-melekh*). The office-title reading sharpens the narrative claim that Yosef now holds the formal vizier-office. ASV-baseline 'the second chariot' retained; documented in the overlay `mirkevet-ha-mishneh-chariot-of-the-second-gen41`.

*Avrekh* (אַבְרֵךְ) — the acclamation cried before Yosef's chariot — is one of the great Egyptological cruxes of the Hebrew Bible, a hapax legomenon of unsettled etymology. Major readings: (a) the **Hebrew kneeling-imperative reading** — 'bow the knee!', taking *avrekh* as a hiphil-derived imperative from *b-r-k* ('to kneel'); the traditional Hebrew etymology (Targumic, rabbinic, KJV/ASV), though the morphology is irregular. (b) The **Egyptian *ib-r-k* acclamation reading** — 'attention!' / 'thou shalt look!' (Spiegelberg; Vergote). (c) The **Egyptian title reading** — *avrekh* as an Egyptian title-shout, 'the vizier!' (various reconstructed Egyptian forms). (d) The **Akkadian *abarakku* reading** — the Akkadian title 'high steward / royal seal-keeper', borrowed into Hebrew (some modern philologists). (e) LXX renders κῆρυξ ('herald'); Vulgate paraphrases 'that all should bow the knee before him'. No scholarly consensus; the entry documents without adjudicating. ASV-baseline 'Bow the knee' retained; the central entry `avrekh-acclamation-egyptological-crux` houses the full crux.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף אֲנִ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וּבִלְעָדֶ֗יךָ לֹֽא־יָרִ֨ים אִ֧ישׁ אֶת־יָד֛וֹ וְאֶת־רַגְל֖וֹ בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh said unto Yosef, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֣ה שֵׁם־יוֹסֵף֮ צָֽפְנַ֣ת פַּעְנֵחַ֒ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֣וֹ אֶת־אָֽסְנַ֗ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֛רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֹ֖ן לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֖ף עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh called Yosef's name Tzafnat-Pa'aneach; and he gave him to wife Asenat, the daughter of Poti-Phera priest of On. And Yosef went out over the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary:
The verse stacks four Egyptian-loanword nodes — the throne-name, the wife's name, the father-in-law's name, and the city — each of which is housed centrally.

*Tzafnat-Pa'aneach* (צָֽפְנַת פַּעְנֵחַ), Pharaoh's throne-name for Yosef, is an Egyptological crux with multiple proposed etymologies and no settled reading: (a) **Eg. *djed-pa-netjer-iw.f-ankh*** ('the god speaks and he lives'), the leading modern reading (Steindorff; Vergote); (b) **Hebrew *tz-f-n* + Egyptian *pa'aneach*** ('revealer of secrets', traditional Targumic and Rashi); (c) various other Egyptian-compound reconstructions (*sopdu-en-paneakh*, etc.). None secure. WoH proper-name transliteration 'Tzafnat-Pa'aneach' retained per established convention; the crux is documented centrally.

*Asenat* (אָֽסְנַת) — Yosef's Egyptian wife, the name commonly read as theophoric *iw.s-n-Nt* ('she belongs to / is dedicated to Neith', the Egyptian creator-goddess); Vergote and standard Egyptological treatments.

*Poti-Phera* (פּוֹטִי פֶרַע), Asenat's father, the priest of On — distinct in MT from *Potifar* (Gen 37:36, 39:1) by the slightly varied vocalization, though both share the Egyptian name-root *pa-di-pa-r'* ('he whom Re gave'). The two names are kept distinct (mainstream modern reading; some rabbinic harmonization identifies them, but this is exegetical, not philological).

*On* (אֹן) — the Egyptian city *iwnw* ('pillar-city'), the Greek **Heliopolis** ('sun-city'), the cult-center of the sun-god Re. The priesthood of On was among the most prestigious in Egypt; Asenat's status as daughter of the priest of On makes her a daughter of the Egyptian solar-cult elite. Cross-corpus reach: Ezek 30:17 (in the form *Aven*); Jer 43:13 (*Beit-Shemesh asher b-eretz Mitzrayim*, 'the house of the sun in the land of Egypt' — the same city).

paragraphs.text: וְיוֹסֵף֙ בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעָמְד֕וֹ לִפְנֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיַּעְבֹ֖ר בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And Yosef was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Mitsrayim. And Yosef went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֣עַשׂ הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֣י הַשָּׂבָ֑ע לִקְמָצִֽים׃

i18n.en: And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.

paragraphs.commentary: *Li-qmatzim* (לִקְמָצִים) — 'by handfuls' — is a rare construction. The noun *qomets* ('handful', from *q-m-tz*, the verb of grasping a handful) elsewhere denotes the priest's *handful* of grain-offering (Lev 2:2; 5:12; 6:8 [MT 6:1]); here the distributive *li-qmatzim* yields two readings: (a) the **literal-distributive reading** — each plant produced 'handfuls' of grain, the abundance-image (ASV/KJV); (b) the **metaphorical reading** — 'in abundance / in heaps / abundantly' (NJPS, NRSV). Chapter-singular construction; documented in the overlay entry.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֞ץ אֶת־כָּל־אֹ֣כֶל ׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּתֶּן־אֹ֖כֶל בֶּעָרִ֑ים אֹ֧כֶל שְׂדֵה־הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְבִיבֹתֶ֖יהָ נָתַ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Mitsrayim, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up in the same.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּצְבֹּ֨ר יוֹסֵ֥ף בָּ֛ר כְּח֥וֹל הַיָּ֖ם הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד עַ֛ד כִּי־חָדַ֥ל לִסְפֹּ֖ר כִּי־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

i18n.en: And Yosef laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left off numbering; for it was without number.

paragraphs.text: וּלְיוֹסֵ֤ף יֻלַּד֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא שְׁנַ֣ת הָרָעָ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And unto Yosef were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenat, the daughter of Poti-Phera priest of On, bare unto him.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם הַבְּכ֖וֹר מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה כִּֽי־נַשַּׁ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־כָּל־עֲמָלִ֔י וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Yosef called the name of the first-born Menasheh: For, said he, Elohim hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house.

paragraphs.commentary: *Menasheh* (מְנַשֶּׁה) — name-aetiology: *ki-nashani Elohim et-kol-amali ve-et kol-beit avi* ('for Elohim hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house'). The verb *nashah* ('to forget') drives the aetiology, with the participial-derivative *menasheh* = 'one who causes forgetting' / 'making to forget'. The aetiology is *Yosef's* declaration in his own mouth — neither endorsed nor disowned by the narrator — and bears the chapter's most theologically loaded clause: that the *father's house* (the brothers, Ya'aqov's household) belongs to the things Yosef has been made to *forget*. The clause is unsettled by the rest of the cycle: Gen 42-50 in fact requires Yosef to remember and reconcile, not forget — but the v 51 declaration stands as the chapter's stated meaning of the birth-name. The name itself becomes one of the dominant tribal designations of the Northern Kingdom material throughout the HB (the half-tribe Menasheh across Joshua 13, 17; Judges; Kings; Chronicles), making the lexeme MANDATORY central.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֛ת שֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י קָרָ֣א אֶפְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־הִפְרַ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ עָנְיִֽי׃

i18n.en: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For Elohim hath made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ephraim* (אֶפְרָיִם) — name-aetiology: *ki-hifrani Elohim be-eretz onyi* ('for Elohim hath made me fruitful in the land of my affliction'). The verb *parah* ('to be fruitful') drives the aetiology; the *be-eretz onyi* phrase ('in the land of my affliction') retains the memory of Yosef's Egyptian-sojourn as affliction even as it names his son for the fruitfulness Elohim has granted there. The two birth-names form a programmatic pair: Menasheh inscribes *forgetting* (the past); Ephraim inscribes *fruitfulness* (the present). Ephraim becomes the dominant Northern-Kingdom tribe across the HB — frequently *Ephraim* stands pars pro toto for the entire Northern Kingdom in prophetic discourse (Isa 7-11; Hos passim; Jer 31:9, 20; the conventional designation of the breakaway kingdom under Yerov'am ben-Nevat). MANDATORY central.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּכְלֶ֕ינָה שֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֣י הַשָּׂבָ֑ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And the seven years of plenty, that was in the land of Mitsrayim, came to an end.

paragraphs.text: וַתְּחִלֶּ֜ינָה שֶׁ֣בַע שְׁנֵ֤י הָרָעָב֙ לָב֔וֹא כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בְּכָל־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת וּבְכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם הָ֥יָה לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: And the seven years of famine began to come, according as Yosef had said: and there was famine in all lands; but in all the land of Mitsrayim there was bread.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּרְעַב֙ כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֛ם אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה לַלָּ֑חֶם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֤ה לְכָל־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְכ֣וּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמַ֥ר לָכֶ֖ם תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃

i18n.en: And when all the land of Mitsrayim was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all Mitsrayim, Go unto Yosef; what he saith to you, do.

paragraphs.text: וְהָרָעָ֣ב הָיָ֔ה עַ֖ל כָּל־פְּנֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶֽת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֣ר לְמִצְרַ֔יִם וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָֽרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: and Yosef opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Mitsrim; and the famine was sore in the land of Mitsrayim.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yiftach Yosef et-kol-asher bahem* — literally 'and Yosef opened all that was in them' — uses an anaphorically loose pronoun *bahem* ('in them') whose antecedent (the storehouses, the granaries, the cities of v 48) is contextually clear but grammatically incomplete. ASV/KJV insert 'storehouses' as a contextual gloss to fill the ellipsis; the literal-preserving alternative ('all that was in them') and the modern gloss ('all the granaries', NJPS) are both available. ASV-baseline retained.

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ בָּ֣אוּ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה לִשְׁבֹּ֖ר אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And all the earth came into Mitsrayim to Yosef to buy grain, because the famine was sore in all the earth.
